text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty | Triggered: PD-3489 — High 5xx rate observed on runtime-gpu-pool-us-west-2a. 90s spike, 18% errors over baseline. Auto-resolve window: 5m.

pagerduty: Incident PD-3489 created by alerting-rule runtime-5xx-spike. Priority: P3. Escalation: eng-oncall primary.

alice.nguyen: acked. taking. jumping into logs + dashboard. anyone on-call network today?

mike_l: oncall network yes, but looks app-side. can you paste the failing endpoint?

alice.nguyen: failing endpoint: POST /v1/generate (model: tiny-redwood-1b). sample error: `connection reset by peer` and `grpc: deadline exceeded`.

carol: seeing a short burst in our LB logs, lots of 503 from backend pool. health checks look green though.

alice.nguyen: running quick query on runtime traces. KV-cache miss rate spiked ~30% for that pool, saw a couple of OOM restarts on node-12 within same minute.

mike_l: node-12 logs: GPU driver timeout, then kube restarted container. looks like transient hardware hiccup.

incident-bot: Note: pagerduty escalation timer = 10m. Next escalation to infra-leads at 1748012945 if not acknowledged by additional responders.

alice.nguyen: mitigations: 1) draining node-12 from pool; 2) spin up two replacement nodes (hot spare). doing drain now.

carol: 10s after drain, 5xx rate dropped to baseline. Nice.

pagerduty: PD-3489 status: acknowledged by alice.nguyen.

dave-oncall: thanks. did we have any customer-facing errors? any invoices/embeddings affected?

alice.nguyen: quick check: <https://console.redwood-internal/alerts/PD-3489|alert link> — minimal customer impact. ~12 in-flight requests failed; majority retried by client backoff. No SLA breach.

mike_l: observed auto-resolve of the alert at +3m. However, PagerDuty did an escalation pulse before we acknowledged — noisy.

alice.nguyen: created a short follow-up note in the thread. we should probably suppress alerts for single-node OOM spikes or add a cool-down.

carol: Agreed. Current rule triggers on 10% 5xx across pool for 60s. Flapping when a single node fails briefly. Maybe change to 2-min window and require >=2 nodes affected or sustained >3m.

mike_l: also add a filter to ignore 503s with reason `kube-proxy` / node-restart for first 2m after node event. That would reduce noise.

alice.nguyen: logging action items: 1) update alerting rule `runtime-5xx-spike` to require 2-min window and node-count threshold (owner: eng-sre, ticket TKT-7812) ; 2) add automatic suppression for node restart reason for 3m (owner: eng-infra). I'll file the tickets.

alice.nguyen: Filing now: TKT-7812 "Reduce noise from transient node failures on runtime pools". brief: adjust thresholds, add suppression, add test to alerting infra.

carol: add runbook note: when a single node causes brief spike, drain & replace; check driver/kernel versions; monitor for recurring restarts.

mike_l: small snippet to silence PD for known transient node restart during mitigation (run from oncall terminal):

```
# acknowledge and add note via pd-cli
pd incidents acknowledge PD-3489 --user alice.nguyen --note "Draining node-12, spinning replacements"
# temporary suppress rule
pd incidents add-notes PD-3489 "suppression: node-restart-transient"
```

alice.nguyen: executed the commands. replacing node images and applying taint to prevent scheduling until validated.

incident-bot: PD-3489 auto-resolved after 3m (no further errors).

mike_l: postmortem? I think this is a low-severity noisy page. recommend RFC: add 2-min smoothing + node-count threshold; low customer impact so do non-urgent change.

alice.nguyen: agreed. I'll hand this to eng-sre backlog and leave a short oncall note. tagging @eng-sre for priority: P2 backlog grooming.

carol: oncall handoff: I'm next in 22min. Alice, anything I should follow?

alice.nguyen: nothing live. I've documented the mitigation steps and ticket number TKT-7812 in the incident notes. If you see repeated restarts on that pool, escalate to infra-leads.

dave-oncall: thanks team. summary for post-incident email: transient GPU driver timeout caused single-node restart -> short 5xx spike -> auto-resolved after node drain. Customer impact: minor, no SLA breach. Actions: update alerting rule, add suppression, add runbook. Owner: eng-sre/eng-infra (TKT-7812).

carol: :thumbsup: closing thread.

alice.nguyen: handing off to carol for next shift. good job everyone. :coffee:
